bluf: Seokratie is a Munich SEO and GEO agency founded in 2008 that sells rankings in Google and visibility in ChatGPT, Claude and AI search to B2B and industrial firms, backed by its own SEO, Google Ads and AI courses. The record shows it practising what it sells: an llms.txt of about 11,600 characters, 17 AI topic URLs, 3 of 3 tested lines corroborated. It is leaning further into GEO and AI consulting, though no dated move is on record. A rival should know its client proof is one testimonial, Clickworker, and a case study page dated 2023-07-27.
doing:
Seokratie positions as a Munich SEO and GEO agency for B2B and industrial firms, promising lasting rankings and visibility in Google and AI search since 2008. Decoded: it gets business to business and industrial companies found, first in Google and now in AI answer engines, and sells longevity as the proof. The headline claim is its title's promise of lasting rankings backed by 16 years of experience.

The sold mix leads with SEO and AI Search / GEO together, both at score 3: the title brands it an SEO agency, the H1 pairs GEO with SEO, the menu lists nine SEO sub services, and a dedicated GEO page sells visibility in ChatGPT, Claude and AI search. The core lines at score 2 are AI Automation (a KI-Beratung, or AI consulting, line plus an AI course for online marketers), B2B & ABM (an H1 aimed at B2B and industry, a GEO page framed around B2B buying centres, a lead generation line), Content & Digital PR (one of four homepage services) and Paid Search (SEA as a homepage core service and a Google Ads course). CRO, creator, email and CRM, paid social and programmatic score 1 with no evidence note; data and measurement scores 0. Proprietary: its own SEO, Google Ads and AI courses and an SEO & SEA Guide, in a knowledge hub with webinars, meetups and an 'SEO für Dummies' book.

AI posture: it sells GEO built on SEO and pitched as a bluff free method, adds AI consulting and courses, and publishes the llms.txt it would sell.

Moves: the record holds none dated. The newest dated items are a case study page from 2023-07-27 and guides stamped 2025-05-02 to 2025-05-06. Pricing: a non binding initial consultation and a free GEO webinar for beginners, no prices shown. Conspicuously absent: named clients, a measurement line, a partner listing and any open role on its Personio board.
clients:
Seokratie sells to a mixed ICP from a single office in Munich, and the record lists its verticals as B2B and industrial and manufacturing. The home market is Germany: the services list is written in German, from SEA-Betreuung to Barrierefreiheit-Check.

The needs read holds 1 client: 0 observed and 1 names only. That client is Clickworker, named in a testimonial on the home page and coded engagement named only, so what it bought is inferred from the sold mix: organic demand and AI visibility, the lines Seokratie leads with. No case study title, press release or URL slug describes the work. The deepen pass counts 4 case studies, and the one dated case study row is the "Erfolge & Case Studies 2023" page from 2023-07-27, whose excerpt says it has worked with clients across many industries and offers a selection of references without naming any. The references exist in its own words; the record simply holds none of the names.

No client is shared with another tracked agency, so the record shows no shopping signal.

What the base needs next: the Horus read places Seokratie best for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) through AI Search / GEO and content. It is likely, moderate confidence, that B2B and industrial buyers researching suppliers in AI answers ask for proof they are cited, and the read finds no audited AI visibility product (P1 partial). It is most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) and KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better) through SEO: a roughly even chance that clients buying rankings start asking what those hours return as clicks give way to citations, with Data & Measurement at 0.
house: Say and do: three lines tested, all practised, and the Horus integrity score reads 100. AI search is corroborated: it publishes an llms.txt, which the record sizes at about 11,600 characters summarising its services for AI crawlers, and its sitemap holds 17 AI topic URLs; no AI crawlers are blocked. LinkedIn advertising is corroborated on a single company page ad, an SEO quick tip on local backlinks and directory listings ("Local Backlinks & Branchenbücher: Bringt's das?"). Publishing cadence is corroborated on the test's terms, yet thin: the compile counts 972 sitemap URLs, 1 updated in 90 days and the same 1 in 365, while the deepen pass read 2312. Paid search is unknown because the Transparency Center lookup was blocked. The tag stack is GTM, GA4 and Google Ads on WordPress: no social pixel, no test tools, no ABM stack. Channels: LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, X and Facebook.
market:
The Horus read puts Seokratie at a tailwind index of 11.9, band Favored, percentile 51. Best placed for KJ1, the click is being replaced by the citation (net 0.322, AI Search / GEO and Content & Digital PR against SEO), and KJ2, ads inside AI answers scale faster than any channel before them (net 0.23, AI Search / GEO and Paid Search). Most exposed to KJ6, the agency middle is being hollowed out (net -0.142, SEO and Paid Search), and KJ9, measurement gets worse before it gets better (net -0.138, SEO). Best scenario fit: The Toll Road at 40/100. It is partial on P1, P4, P6 and P7, absent on P2 and P8, unknown on P5, and makes none in full; P3 does not apply.

The Monsoon read is 50.5, band Breeze, percentile 30: migration 49.0 against displacement 52.0, inferred. SEO (14) and AI Search / GEO (7) carry the most movable hours; the work would go 55% to Eastern Europe and 35% to South and Southeast Asia. No hub office and no onshore claim is listed.
openings:
The strongest opening is proof. Seokratie sells lasting rankings and B2B visibility in AI search, yet the record names 1 client, Clickworker, through a testimonial with no described work, and its case study page is dated 2023-07-27. A rival with dated, named results for B2B and industrial firms in Germany is likely, moderate confidence, to win the reference stage against it. Falsifier: dated case studies naming industrial clients on seokratie.de in the next compile.

The GEO line is practised but not measured: an llms.txt and 17 AI topic URLs, yet no audited AI visibility product (P1 partial), no feed, schema or entity work (P2 absent) and Data & Measurement at 0. An offer that reports citation share for industrial buyers is likely to undercut it on the line it leads with.

It runs paid search with no sign of testing ads inside AI assistants (P8 absent), a gap under KJ2, a judgment it is placed for. Its KJ6 exposure runs through SEO hours, and with displacement at 52.0 on the Monsoon read, a price attack is a roughly even chance lever, low confidence. There is no public pricing model (P5 unknown).
watch: Indicator I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, next reading late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization of the Google rankings it sells, while above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and its KJ1 tailwind.

Indicator I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the $2B milestone and pricing below $20 CPM decide whether KJ2 pays off for an agency that sells paid search and GEO but tests no ads inside assistants.

Indicator I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, next reading October 2026: output or outcome pricing at a top five holdco would sharpen KJ6, the judgment its SEO hours are most exposed to.

Indicator I10, Reddit US daily users versus search referral volatility, next reading late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.
The references behind the 2023-07-27 case study page and the 4 case studies the deepen pass counts: named, dated results in the next compile would lift the book above one testimonial.
The next Radar compile: this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile, and a Transparency Center lookup that is not blocked would settle whether it runs the Google ads it sells.
